name: Ship a change
description: Do a piece of work in a repository, open a pull request for it, then hand that pull request to the `pr-babysitter` workflow and let it drive the PR to green.

inputs.name: task
inputs.description: What to change in the repository.

inputs.name: cwd
inputs.description: Checkout to work in, relative to the workspace.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: owner/name the pull request belongs to. Empty means the checkout's own remote.

nodes.name: Do the work and open a PR

config.prompt:
="Work in the checkout at " + .inputs.cwd + ", which is where the next step looks for the pull request — an agent step starts at the workspace root, not there.

Work on the following task:

" + .inputs.task + "

Create a branch, implement it, run the repository's own build, lint and test commands until they pass, and commit. Push the branch and open a pull request against the upstream default branch with `gh pr create` — ready for review, not a draft. Do not merge it. Finish by printing the pull request URL on its own line."

args.script:
set -u
repo_arg=""
[ -n "${REPO:-}" ] && repo_arg="--repo ${REPO}"

# No argument: `gh pr view` resolves the PR for the branch that is checked
# out, which is the one the agent just pushed.
#
# Two very different failures hide behind the same exit code here. "No pull
# request for this branch" is a real answer — the agent did not open one — and
# routes to the `no_pr` branch. A missing `gh`, a bad token, or the wrong repo
# is a host problem, and blaming the agent for it would send someone reading
# this report looking in entirely the wrong place. So the message decides.
# `gh --jq` builds the whole document, so this step never has to pick a
# delimiter and split on it — there is nothing to get wrong in a URL that
# contains almost any character you might have chosen.
#
# `pr` is a string, not a number: the babysitter declares it as a string input
# and the child validates what arrives against its own declaration.
if out=$(gh pr view $repo_arg --json number,url --jq '{pr: (.number | tostring), url: .url, found: true}' 2>&1); then
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
else
  case "$out" in
    *"no pull requests found"*|*"no open pull requests"*)
      printf '{"pr":"","url":"","found":false}\n' ;;
    *)
      printf 'cannot look up the pull request for this branch: %s\n' "$out" >&2
      exit 1 ;;
  esac
fi

set.note: ="the agent did not leave an open pull request on the checked-out branch: " + (.nodes.implement.item.text // "no output")
